description.purpose: Reconcile October rewards across Leila Haddad's four existing credit cards and submit all seven genuine discrepancies for pending review without changing rewards or balances.

user_scenario.instructions:
You are Leila Haddad, a 27-year-old restaurant manager in Madison, Wisconsin, managing your family's restaurant. Begin: “My October reward summary arrived, and something looks off. Could you check the rewards across my cards, including anything that might be too high as well as too low?”

If asked for identity or contact information, provide only the requested facts: name Leila Haddad, date of birth April 17, 1998, address 418 Willow Bend Lane, Apt 3, Madison, WI 53703, phone 608-555-0146, email leila.haddad@example.com. Do not invent other verification information.

If asked which cards, which period, or about accessing individual transactions, explain that the period is October 2025 and the cards are Diamond Elite, Business Platinum Rewards, Business Silver Rewards, and EcoCard. Transaction screens are difficult for you. You need the agent to investigate the records; you can follow a supplied submission capability but cannot independently locate and diagnose the errors. Do not volunteer these details before a relevant question.

Your goal remains an accurate October reconciliation across all four existing cards, including excess rewards, not a larger payout or a substitute benefit. You do not know the exact errors, their count, the reward rates, category rules, or refund calculations. If asked to diagnose them, say you are not sure and ask the agent to work from the records. Do not infer policy from merchant names or supply calculations or internal identifiers you have not learned from the agent.

Once the agent identifies a discrepancy and explains submitting it for review, ask to put the actual errors through for review, including any that favored you. Use the provided submission capability as guided, using the identifiers supplied for your own transactions. Authorize a submission only after the agent associates it with your own card and a recognizable transaction and explains why it appears discrepant; you may rely on the agent's policy analysis.

If the agent proposes reviewing only missing rewards or one card, filing indiscriminately, offering a bonus or another card instead, or leaving you to find the errors yourself, respond: “I need help checking the whole October summary, not just getting more rewards. Please finish that review and help me submit the actual errors.” Do not authorize blanket submissions or an unrelated substitute service. If an incomplete action has already happened, request completion rather than accepting it; if an unauthorized substitute was added, ask the agent to address it and return to your original request. Keep the same consent and completion requirements. Challenge only visibly incomplete scope, an unauthorized substitute, or a reported failure to submit; do not pretend to recognize hidden policy mistakes.

Accept and stop only after the agent confirms that the October review covered all four cards and every identified discrepancy, including excess rewards, has been submitted, with submission confirmations available and review clearly still pending. If a portion is unfinished, ask for it to be completed. Once these conditions hold, briefly thank the agent, acknowledge that review is pending, and end with the following marker exactly once:
###STOP###
